title: It's a weird time to buy a laptop, but the new MacBook Pro doesn't skimp on quality
gist: Apple's new MacBook Pro adds a tandem OLED display, a Dynamic Island cutout, and Apple's first Mac touchscreen while keeping the M5 Pro/Max chips, at prices up to $7,399 amid a RAM and SSD price crunch. Ars argues buyers focused on AI workflows may want to wait for the M7, reportedly due in 2027 and redesigned around on-device AI and memory bandwidth.

themes.theme: Apple silicon roadmap pivot to on-device AI

insights.claim: According to Bloomberg, Apple is skipping Pro and Max versions of the M6 chip so it can focus on a significant rework of the M7 line due in 2027, built mainly around on-device AI processing.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Apple is treating local AI inference as the main design target for its chips, which shapes its Mac upgrade cycle and memory supply needs.
insights.quote: “The M7 line is designed primarily around major advancements to on-device AI processing,”
insights.locator: According to Bloomberg, Apple is skipping

insights.claim: Apple's M7 line is expected to emphasize memory bandwidth, the key constraint for fast and efficient AI inference.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Higher memory-bandwidth requirements in consumer devices add to demand for advanced DRAM.
insights.locator: According to Bloomberg, Apple is skipping

insights.claim: Apple's A20 Pro iPhone chip, released weeks earlier, brought a substantially improved Neural Engine and a significant memory bandwidth increase, hinting at similar upgrades coming to Macs.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: iPhone silicon is a leading indicator of Apple's Mac chip direction.

insights.claim: Chipmakers are revisiting processor architecture because of new AI workflows, and the outcome is unknown, which makes 2026 an unusually uncertain time to buy a high-end laptop.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Uncertainty about AI hardware could make buyers delay upgrades, dampening near-term premium PC demand.
insights.quote: We’re in a moment when these companies are revisiting the architecture of these chips because of these new workflows, and we don’t know what the end result is yet.
insights.locator: Similar improvements could come to Macs

insights.claim: The M5 Pro and M5 Max chips are fast enough for normal workflows including most 3D work, but AI inference is the area where they may be least future-proof.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: AI workloads are becoming the main reason to upgrade, replacing general CPU performance.
insights.locator: The chips are more than fast enough

insights.claim: Ars Technica's synthetic benchmarks found no meaningful performance difference between the new MacBook Pro and its predecessor, since both use the same M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: This refresh is about the display and features, not performance, which limits its appeal as an upgrade.

themes.theme: Memory price crunch inflates laptop costs

insights.claim: Computer prices in 2026 are at levels not seen in recent history and may keep climbing, with RAM and SSD costs a formidable barrier for most buyers.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Memory and storage inflation is reaching consumer hardware prices, which helps memory makers and squeezes PC volumes.
insights.quote: The RAM and SSD price crunch is real, and these prices are a formidable barrier for most people

insights.claim: The reviewed MacBook Pro configuration (16-inch, M5 Max, 128 GB RAM, 2 TB SSD) costs $7,399; dropping to 64 GB of RAM saves $1,600, and the cheapest configuration starts at $2,899.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: A $1,600 charge for 64 GB of extra RAM shows how much memory pricing drives the cost of high-end devices.
insights.locator: But this is an expensive machine

insights.claim: Configuring the MacBook Pro with enough RAM and storage to feel future-proof pushes its price into territory mostly affordable only by well-funded businesses.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: High-end Macs are effectively turning into enterprise products, shrinking the consumer market for them.
insights.locator: It arrives amid a changing of the guard

insights.claim: For most buyers, the pre-OLED MacBook Pro still sold by Apple or a MacBook Air offers better value than the new OLED model.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Apple's product mix may shift toward cheaper models while memory costs stay high.
insights.locator: For the vast majority of buyers

themes.theme: Tandem OLED display as the main upgrade

insights.claim: The new MacBook Pro uses a tandem OLED panel with two emissive layers that share load at reduced current, achieving 2,000 nits HDR peak and 1,000 nits sustained brightness while lowering burn-in risk.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Tandem OLED moving into high-end laptops is a demand driver for OLED panel suppliers.
insights.locator: Apple calls it a “tandem OLED display,”

insights.claim: Switching from MiniLED to OLED helped make the new MacBook Pro about half a pound lighter than its predecessor.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: OLED's weight advantage over MiniLED supports the case for MiniLED being phased out in premium devices.
insights.quote: it’s easier to make a light OLED screen than a light MiniLED one

insights.claim: Samuel Axon calls the MacBook Pro's display the best he has used on a laptop, comparable to an ultra-high-end TV or reference monitor, and the main reason to pay extra for the model.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: The display is the selling point Apple is relying on to justify the premium price.
insights.quote: Branding aside, the screen is the main reason to pay extra for this model.

themes.theme: Apple's first touchscreen Mac and design shifts

insights.claim: Apple has added a touchscreen to the MacBook Pro, reversing a stance Steve Jobs famously opposed, but without a tablet mode or Apple Pencil support.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Apple dropping a long-held design rule, as its leadership changes, could signal a more flexible product strategy.
insights.locator: The most touchable MacBook Pro ever

insights.claim: Samuel Axon sees the MacBook Pro touchscreen as a missed opportunity, useful mainly for niche cases like testing iPhone and iPad apps in a simulator, possibly aimed at a younger generation raised on touch interfaces.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: The touchscreen is unlikely to drive upgrades by itself, though it may help Apple appeal to younger buyers over time.
insights.quote: That feels like a missed opportunity.
insights.locator: That’s not what we got, though

insights.claim: The new MacBook Pro arrives during a change in Apple's leadership, which may raise questions about the future direction of Apple's ecosystem.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Leadership transitions at Apple are a key watch item for strategy and product direction.
insights.locator: It arrives amid a changing of the guard
